scope: Three short reviews of the new classroom readings on rulers, religion, burial and writing. Use the whole-unit forms for the rest of the Egypt material.

pool.prompt: What does a double crown on a pharaoh’s statue suggest?
options: The ruler claimed authority over Upper and Lower Egypt
The ruler led only Lower Egypt
The figure worked as a scribe
The statue was carved from granite
pool.rationale: The double crown combined the white crown of Upper Egypt and red crown of Lower Egypt.

pool.prompt: A museum label identifies a red crown. Which region should the label name?
options: Upper Egypt
Lower Egypt
Both regions
The Valley of the Kings
pool.rationale: The red crown represented Lower Egypt. The white crown represented Upper Egypt.

pool.prompt: An artist gives a pharaoh a crook and flail. What do these objects help communicate?
options: The pharaoh’s writing skill
The route of the Nile
The pharaoh’s authority
The year the statue was made
pool.rationale: The crook and flail are royal symbols of authority.

pool.prompt: How did Hatshepsut connect her rule to religion in the obelisk reading?
options: She credited a treaty with the Hittites
She claimed the obelisk was her tomb
She used the Greek version of a decree
She presented Amun as supporting her rule
pool.rationale: The inscription links Hatshepsut’s authority to the god Amun.

pool.prompt: What is an obelisk?
options: A tall four-sided monument that narrows toward the top
An oval border around a royal name
A curved royal staff
A rock-cut tomb
pool.rationale: An obelisk is a tall, narrowing monument. Hatshepsut used one to record claims about her rule.

pool.prompt: What could a historian learn directly from the writing on Hatshepsut’s obelisk?
options: How many possessions were buried with Tutankhamun
How she wanted people to understand her right to rule
What the Hittites agreed to with Ramses II
Why Roman leaders opposed Cleopatra
pool.rationale: The inscription tells us how Hatshepsut presented her own authority.

pool.prompt: Which achievement shows Ramses II using diplomacy?
options: Building a stone monument
Wearing a royal crown
Making a peace agreement with the Hittites
Preparing a royal burial
pool.rationale: Diplomacy includes negotiating an agreement. The treaty is evidence of diplomacy.

pool.prompt: Which ruler is associated with major building projects and a treaty with the Hittites?
options: Tutankhamun
Cleopatra VII
Menes
Ramses II
pool.rationale: Ramses II is remembered for major monuments and a peace treaty with the Hittites.

pool.prompt: A temple and a peace agreement show two sides of Ramses II’s rule. Which pair fits?
options: Construction and diplomacy
Embalming and worship
Deciphering and recordkeeping
Farming and irrigation
pool.rationale: A temple is a building project. A peace agreement reflects diplomacy.

pool.prompt: Why is Tutankhamun especially well known today?
options: He signed the Hittite peace treaty
His tomb was found with many objects still inside
He built Khufu’s pyramid
He negotiated with Julius Caesar
pool.rationale: The objects found in his tomb in 1922 made him widely known.

pool.prompt: Which ruler made alliances with Roman leaders to help keep power in Egypt?
options: Hatshepsut
Ramses II
Cleopatra VII
Tutankhamun
pool.rationale: Cleopatra worked with Julius Caesar and later Mark Antony while Roman power was growing.

pool.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a ruler with evidence from the gallery?
options: Cleopatra VII and the Hittite peace treaty
Ramses II and the unification double crown
Menes and the Rosetta Stone decree
Tutankhamun and his gold burial mask
pool.rationale: The gold mask is one of the objects recovered from Tutankhamun’s tomb.

pool.prompt: Which god was associated with funerals and embalming?
options: Anubis
Ra
Horus
Thoth
pool.rationale: The class notes associate Anubis with preparing the dead and with funerals.

pool.prompt: Which two associations match the religion notes?
options: Ra with chaos and Seth with the sun
Ma’at with order and Thoth with wisdom
Anubis with the sky and Horus with embalming
Osiris with cats and Bastet with the afterlife
pool.rationale: Ma’at was associated with truth and order, and Thoth with wisdom.

pool.prompt: Which god was most closely associated with the underworld and afterlife in the notes?
options: Ra
Thoth
Osiris
Horus
pool.rationale: Osiris was associated with the underworld and the afterlife.

pool.prompt: Why did Egyptians place personal objects in some tombs?
options: They were trying to make the mummy dry faster
They used tomb goods to measure the Nile flood
They wanted to identify the king’s crown colors
They believed the dead could use possessions in the afterlife
pool.rationale: Burial objects reflect beliefs about what a person might need after death.

pool.prompt: Which step came before wrapping the body in linen in the classroom notes?
options: Removing moisture from the body
Closing the coffin
Putting the coffin in the tomb
Covering the tomb entrance
pool.rationale: Drying helped preserve the body before it was wrapped.

pool.prompt: Which statement connects mummification to a religious belief?
options: Preparing the body helped scribes count crops
Preparing the body helped ready the dead for the afterlife
Wrapping the body marked Upper Egypt on a map
Putting objects in a tomb decoded hieroglyphs
pool.rationale: The class notes explain preservation as preparation for the afterlife.

pool.prompt: Why might a scribe use hieratic for everyday records?
options: It required carving every word into stone
It was the Greek version of the Egyptian language
Its simpler strokes made writing quicker
It could only be used for a royal name
pool.rationale: Hieratic simplified the signs into faster strokes, which suited recordkeeping.

pool.prompt: What does a cartouche mark in an Egyptian inscription?
options: A river boundary
The beginning of a farming season
The end of a trade route
A royal name
pool.rationale: The oval border encloses a royal name.

pool.prompt: Which three forms of writing are on the Rosetta Stone?
options: Hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Greek
Hieroglyphs, hieratic, and Latin
Demotic, hieratic, and cuneiform
Greek, Latin, and cuneiform
pool.rationale: The stone repeats the decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek scripts.

pool.prompt: Why did the Greek version of the Rosetta Stone help scholars?
options: It pictured the exact tools used to carve every sign
They could read it and compare it with the Egyptian versions
It gave each Egyptian ruler a separate map
It supplied a list of modern English letters
pool.rationale: A known script gave scholars a way to compare parallel versions of the same message.

pool.prompt: Which artifact would best support a claim that Egyptians used different scripts for different purposes?
options: Two identical copies of a Greek map
A gold mask displayed next to a coffin
A quick hieratic supply record alongside a carved hieroglyphic inscription
Two pottery jars with no writing
pool.rationale: The different texts show how the writing styles fit different tasks.

pool.prompt: What does a cartouche on a monument give a historian a clue to?
options: The date the Nile first flooded that year
The number of workers who quarried the stone
The exact route used to move the stone
The royal name recorded on that monument
pool.rationale: The cartouche identifies a royal name. Its presence alone does not supply the construction details.
